instruction.text: Read the text and answer the following questions.

atoms.text: Sometimes, people don’t voluntarily leave a place but are forced to leave for political or social reasons. This can be applied to many Black Americans who left the South in two waves. The first wave was from around 1910-1940 and the second from 1940-1970. These were two of the largest domestic migrations in US history.

Around 1910, most Black Americans lived in the South, where many enslaved people had been forced to live and work for generations. Even after the emancipation of enslaved Black Americans, many individuals decided to stay in the same area. Yet, by the year 1940, approximately 1.5 million Black Americans left their homes. By 1970, just over 50% of Black Americans lived in the South. Many individuals migrated to Northern States such as Illinois, Michigan, Pennsylvania or New York, while others moved to Western States.

hint.text:
Emancipation: the act of freeing oneself from the control of someone else.

The Emancipation Proclamation was issued by President Abraham Lincoln on January 1, 1863. It declared the freedom of enslaved people in the Confederate states.
hint.label: Glossary

atoms.text: In the early 1900s, Black Americans were confronted with an illusory system called sharecropping. After the Civil War was over and because the 13th amendment had abolished slavery, many slaveholder farmers were no longer allowed to enslave their workers. Because of that, these farmers thought of a different way to plant and harvest crops on their land. Farmers brought in cheap labour (such as recently enslaved or poor white people) and supplied these workers with a number of things: land, seeds, tools, animals and a place to sleep. The workers were required to work on the farm to the end of the harvest season, and all the things provided were only rented. This was the concept of sharecropping.

hint.text: illusory - creating an illusion; deceptive or misleading
hint.label: Glossary

atoms.text: If a given farmer wasn’t happy with the outcome of the crops, they were able to claim that the workers owed them more. This led to high interest rates and these workers being legally bound to the farmer until they were able to give the farmer what was expected. However, many sharecroppers eventually found themselves in a vicious cycle of endless debt because of spikes in interest rates and unpredictability of harvest seasons. Laws had even been enforced that forced sharecroppers to stay on the land until they were able to settle their debt to the farmer.

hint.text: interest rate - the cost of borrowing. Interest is money or goods to be paid back on top of what was originally borrowed.
hint.label: Glossary

atoms.text: Even in the case of Black Americans who owned their own land, the unpredictability of harvest seasons was a difficult obstacle. Extreme weather and the Boll Weevil pest hindered profitable crops. Black Americans in the South either earned virtually nothing or were in great debt, and, as a result, some began heading up North. Here, jobs in the automobile, meat packing and steel and iron industries were available and paid.

hint.text: The Boll Weevil - historically the largest pest that cotton plants in the southern states suffered from.
hint.label: Glossary

atoms.text: Apart from the economic reasons, like better-paying jobs, there was another reason for the migration from the South to the North: the impact of the so-called Jim Crow laws and domestic terrorism by groups like the Ku Klux Klan. Many white Americans at the time had a problem with the Reconstruction Amendments, which allowed all Black Americans freedom from slavery and full citizenship, and Black American males the right to vote. Jim Crow laws were adopted to segregate Black communities and prevent them from accessing certain resources. Black Americans weren’t even allowed to use the same toilets, water fountains and hospitals as white Americans.

hint.text: to segregate - in this context, means separating one part of society from the other.
hint.label: Glossary

atoms.text: Shortly after the implementation of Jim Crow laws, violent attacks on the Black community increased. At the beginning of the 20th century, there was a significant amount of people who wished to maintain white supremacy. This resulted in more beatings, harassing and lynching of Black people. Given that these violent occurrences became more common, an increasing number of Black people saw their lives in danger and decided to flee to the North. Even though many Black Americans did not wish to leave their homes, economic opportunity and safety became a priority. In the North and West, they were able to live more peacefully than in the South and to continue to fight for their rights as US citizens.

hint.text: white supremacy - a racist belief that people who are white are better than everyone else
hint.label: Glossary

atoms.a: Why did the Great Migration take place in the 20th century? Select the best summary.
b: ++Black Americans living in the South were being excluded both politically and socially.
Northern states politely asked Black Americans to move up north.
Sharecropping regulations were less extreme in the northern states.

atoms.a: What is meant with sharecropping in this context?
b: ++when one person farms another person’s land
when a person legally steals another person’s time and work
when cheap labour asks to work for someone else
